title: EduWild: How Teacher-Configured Chatbots Fail in Real-World Use and How to Fix Them
abstract: arXiv:2610.23530v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Teachers increasingly configure educational chatbots through natural-language instructions, but how these bots fail in real-world use remains poorly understood. We introduce EduWild, a dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, each paired with the instructions and configuration behind it, including 900 conversations from the intended end users of 35 deployed chatbots. We develop a 29-code taxonomy covering factual, workflow, diagnostic, and pedagogical failures and apply it using a human-calibrated LLM judge. The most frequent failures are lapses in following teacher intent --- bots skip required workflow steps (53.8% of end-user conversations), omit expectation setup (33.4%), and overload learners with information or questions (37.1%). translated_title: EduWild：教师配置的聊天机器人在真实使用中如何失败以及如何修复
translated_abstract: 教师越来越多地通过自然语言指令来配置教育聊天机器人，但这些机器人在实际使用中如何失败仍知之甚少。我们推出了EduWild数据集，包含与217个教师配置聊天机器人的1,726段对话，每个机器人都配有其背后的指令和配置信息，其中包括来自35个已部署聊天机器人的预期最终用户的900段对话。我们开发了一个涵盖事实性、工作流程、诊断和教学失败的29类编码分类体系，并使用经过人工校准的LLM评估器进行标注。最常见的失败是未能遵循教师意图——机器人跳过必需的工作流程步骤（占最终用户对话的53.8%）、遗漏期望设置（33.4%），以及用信息或问题使学习者过载（37.1%）。基于这些发现，我们设计了一个针对六种最常见失败模式的基于提示词的干预框架。在一项涉及200名大学生和十个机器人的研究中，该框架减少……
tldr: 该研究通过包含1,726段对话和217个教师配置聊天机器人的EduWild数据集，揭示了此类机器人在真实使用中最常因未遵循教师意图而失败（如跳过工作流程步骤、遗漏期望设置、信息过载），并据此设计了一个基于提示词的干预框架来减少六种最常见失败模式。
en_tdlr: Using the EduWild dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, this study shows that such bots most often fail by not following teacher intent—skipping workflow steps, omitting expectation setup, and overloading learners—and introduces a prompt-based harness that targets the six most frequent failure modes.
